Hi Olga,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Nimbus is preparing an RFP for a dedicated inference pool to support two production workloads:

- Low-latency chat (context up to ~4k tokens) for our customer-facing assistant (p95 latency target ~120ms).
- Large-batch embedding generation for nightly analytics (throughput-oriented).

We attached the RFP with expected QPS / token shapes. Two questions to help us shortlist:

1) For the chat workload, does H100 materially outperform A100 in perf/$ when you include required memory (80GB vs 40/80 options)?
2) For embeddings (float16 large-batch), is L40S a better perf/$ play vs older A100s?

We're also trying to size a 12-month commit with a target of 1.2M generated tokens/day across workloads and need a rough committed spend band to take to procurement. Any ballpark numbers or a simple 3-option packaging (conservative / typical / aggressive) would help.

Alex — quick high-level guidance based on the shapes you gave. I'll keep this short and practical.

Key tradeoffs (summary):
- H100: best raw latency for autoregressive chat and highest perf for large batch fp16, but comes at a higher $/GPU. H100 shines with long contexts + KV cache locality; at p95 latency targets ~120ms it reduces headroom required in the pool.
- A100 (80GB): solid all-rounder, lower capex/commit cost than H100. For chat at moderate context sizes it can meet SLOs with more replicas (higher pool size).
- L40S: very cost-effective for dense fp16 embedding throughput; excellent perf/$ for single-pass embedding jobs but less ideal for chat unless quantized variants are acceptable.

Suggested 3-option packaging (12-month commit) — ballpark monthly committed spend ranges and recommended pool composition:

1) Conservative (cost-first):~$45k / month commit
   - 6x A100-80GB (pool handles chat with higher queueing; expect p95 ~180–230ms)
   - 8x L40S for nightly embeddings (cheapest perf/$)
   - Throughput SLO: best-effort, burst to hosted tier

2) Balanced (recommended initial):~$85k / month commit
   - 4x H100 for chat (low-latency slice) + 4x A100 for mixed traffic
   - 6x L40S for embeddings (batching to maximize perf/$)
   - Throughput SLO: p95 chat ~120–140ms with 5% allowed invocation queueing; nightly embeddings finish within 3 hours

3) Aggressive (performance-first):~$140k / month commit
   - 8x H100 dedicated to chat (headroom for spikes)
   - 4x A100 for background and tooling
   - 8x L40S for embeddings (fastest nightly completion)
   - Throughput SLO: p95 chat <120ms, strict SLAs and dedicated burst capacity

Discount framing: tiered commit discounts apply to hosted rates; typical starting concession for a 12-month commit is 18–28% depending on total spend and optional SLA credits. We can structure ramping credits if Nimbus wants lower entry cost.

Operational notes:
- Mix architecture: we recommend routing by policy (latency-critical → H100 pool, batch jobs → L40S cluster). That lets you balance perf/$ and reserve H100 capacity for p95-sensitive traffic.
- Failover: Redwood can fallback chat requests to A100 variants if H100 capacity is exhausted; we can codify a p95-preserving policy for critical endpoints.

I'm attaching a lightweight config sketch with throughput assumptions and a sample math worksheet (pricing-example-nimbus-draft.xlsx) so procurement can see numbers. Marcus, feel free to add perf details.

— Vivek
VP, Product — Redwood Inference

Alex, quick perf-engineering color to supplement Vivek's guidance:

- For open-llm v2-style chat with aggressive KV cache, H100 shows ~1.6–1.9x lower median token latency vs A100-80GB for the same sequence length; p95 gains are larger in presence of cache hits.
- Memory: if you need to run many concurrent sessions with long context, 80GB A100 is competitive but requires more replicas. H100 reduces replica count at cost of higher unit price.
- L40S: excellent for embedding throughput; when you batch to ~4k sequences, L40S yields the best throughput per-dollar in our tests.

Operational recommendation: start with Vivek's Balanced plan. We'll instrument a 4-week pilot with mixed workloads and telemetry flags that capture p95 latency and token-per-second per GPU. After the pilot we'll recommend a resizing (scale up H100 or reallocate to A100) before final commit.

— Marcus
